cards.explanation: The answer is that God drove them out with His hand. The psalm says, “With Your hand You drove out the nations and planted our fathers there; You crushed the peoples and cast them out.” So God did the driving out AND the planting. I think that's a heavy verse, since it speaks of peoples being crushed. The singers are crediting God's hand for all of it (Psalm 44:2).

The answer is False. The song says, “…it was not by their sword that they took the land; their arm did not bring them victory.” The credit goes to God's right hand, His arm and the light of His face. The singers don't hold onto any of it for themselves, friends (Psalm 44:3).

The answer is that He favored them. The psalm ends that verse with “…because You favored them.” The reason is on God's side, not theirs, friends. The singers don't list any other reason, so I won't make one up either (Psalm 44:3).

The answer is God and His name. The psalmist says, “Through You we repel our foes; through Your name we trample our enemies.” Every win in that verse runs through God. This guy isn't counting on anything he could carry in his own hands (Psalm 44:5).

The answer is confident praise to God. They say God saves them from their enemies, and they sing, “In God we have boasted all day long, and Your name we will praise forever.” That's a confident song, friends. The singers are looking at what God has done and cheering for Him (Psalm 44:7-8).

The answer is False. The psalm says, “You have made us retreat from the foe, and those who hate us have plundered us.” So they're the ones backing away, friends. The song's mood has done a full turnaround (Psalm 44:10).

The answer is nothing. The psalm says, “You sell Your people for nothing; no profit do You gain from their sale.” Nothing changes hands. It's a hard line, friends, and I think it's meant to sting (Psalm 44:12).

The answer is False. The psalm says, “You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to those around us.” The neighbors are mocking them. I think it hurts a lot more when it's the people living right next door (Psalm 44:13).

The answer is disgrace. The psalmist says, “All day long my disgrace is before me…” Same “…all day long…” as the boasting, friends, but now it's carrying shame. Same stretch of hours, very different song (Psalm 44:8, 15).

The answer is False. The psalmist says, “All this has come upon us, though we have not forgotten You or betrayed Your covenant.” That “though” is carrying a lot, friends. The singers say they stayed faithful and the trouble came anyway (Psalm 44:17).

The answer is deepest darkness. The psalmist says, “But You have crushed us in the lair of jackals; You have covered us with deepest darkness.” A lair of jackals is a rough place to be, friends. And the darkness is covering them, not just brushing past (Psalm 44:19).

The answer is True. The psalmist says, “…would not God have discovered, since He knows the secrets of the heart?” So if they'd forgotten God's name or spread out their hands to a foreign god, God would have found out. That's the claim the psalmist is making here, friends (Psalm 44:20-21).

The answer is for God's sake. The psalmist says, “Yet for Your sake we face death all day long…” The “Your” there is God, friends. Whatever they're facing, they say it's on account of Him (Psalm 44:22).

The answer is wake up and arise. He says, “Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise! Do not reject us forever.” He's loud, he's honest, and he's still talking to God. I think that's what faithfulness sounds like when it's hurting, friends (Psalm 44:23).
The answer is True. The psalmist asks, “Why do You hide Your face and forget our affliction and oppression?” He's not hiding the question, friends. He puts it right in front of God (Psalm 44:24).

The answer is dust. The psalmist says, “For our soul has sunk to the dust; our bodies cling to the earth.” That's about as low as a person can get. I think this one is heavy, friends, since it's the sound of people worn all the way down (Psalm 44:25).

The answer is God's loving devotion. The psalmist ends with, “Rise up; be our help! Redeem us on account of Your loving devotion.” He's leaning on who God is, not on how they've done. That's a solid place to land when you're down in the dust, friends (Psalm 44:26).
